units.title: The Italian
units.why: About one White game in eight goes into this line, and you have won only five of the last twelve. One idea runs through all of it: a big center, a quick castle, and every piece aimed at f7.

idea.t: Your bishop points at the pawn beside Black's king. Only the king defends it, and almost every trick in this unit lands there.

idea.h: Small pawn, then the big center
idea.t: The small c-pawn move prepares the d-pawn push. After the trade, two pawns stand side by side in the middle and kick Black's pieces around.
When Black grabs your e-pawn, don't defend anything. Castle: your rook comes to the open file while Black's king is still in the middle.
If Black's bishop keeps grabbing, your other bishop stops Black from ever castling. Let the corner rook go; the king pays for it.

quiz.label: Small pawn, big plan
quiz.note: Push the c-pawn one square. It prepares the d-pawn push, so you can stand two pawns side by side in the center.

quiz.label: Strike the center
quiz.note: Push now. The pawn attacks Black's bishop and center pawn at the same time.

quiz.label: Block with the knight
quiz.rule: Block with the knight, offer the pawn
quiz.note: Block with the knight and offer your e-pawn. If Black takes it, you castle and attack while Black's king is still in the middle. The engine calls the gambit roughly equal, but Black has to find several exact moves to prove it.

quiz.label: Castle!
quiz.note: Castle and let Black keep the pawn. Your king is safe, your rook is about to use the open e-file, and Black's king is still in the middle. Black now has two ways to take your knight.

quiz.label: Bishop blocks castling
quiz.note: The key move. Don't save the rook. Your bishop now stops Black from ever castling, because the king would have to cross a square it attacks.

quiz.label: The Møller push
quiz.note: Push the d-pawn. It attacks Black's knight, and the bishop that took your knight can wait. This move is the heart of the whole line.

units.title: The Slav setup
units.kicker: Black · one setup against the d-pawn
units.why: A third of your Black games start with the d-pawn, and you have lost more of them than you have won. From now on it is one setup, in one order, every time: d-pawn, c-pawn, bishop out, then the e-pawn.

idea.t: Meet the d-pawn with yours and guard it with the c-pawn. The road for your light bishop stays open.

idea.h: Bishop out, then close the door
idea.t: The bishop leaves before the e-pawn moves. Then the three pawns make a triangle that is hard to attack, and the bishop is outside it.
King's knight, light bishop, e-pawn, queen's knight, dark bishop, castle. The pieces go to the same squares in every line, and when two move orders reach the same position your next move is the same.

If White plays the small e-pawn move before bringing a piece out, your bishop goes first and the king's knight waits until after the queen's knight. From home it leaves your queen guarding the edge square, so White's knight can't chase your bishop.

idea.h: When the e-pawn arrives, take it
idea.t: White's one active idea is the e-pawn push. Take it at once and trade knights. One square further and it would fork your bishop and knight.

idea.h: The same squares against the London
idea.t: Against the London the dark bishop comes out straight after the e-pawn and offers a trade. If White takes, the queen takes back, every time.
When the bishops come off and White's queen takes back, she can check your king and hit your b-pawn in one move. The c-pawn shuts that out, and it is the same triangle again.

quiz.label: Bishop out before the e-pawn
quiz.note: The one time the bishop goes before the king's knight. White has no piece out, so nothing can punish it, and if you wait White's bishop takes this diagonal first.

quiz.label: Queen's knight next
quiz.note: After the bishop and the e-pawn, the queen's knight always comes next. While your king's knight is at home your queen guards the edge square, so White's knight can't go there to chase your bishop.

quiz.label: Dark bishop to its square
quiz.note: The same square as in the first lesson, and the same position. Castle next. Equal: no weak pawns and no bad bishop.

quiz.label: Take back with the c-pawn
quiz.rule: Pawn trade: take back with the c-pawn
quiz.note: The position is symmetrical. Your knight will stand in front of the c-pawn's old square.

quiz.label: Offer the dark bishops
quiz.note: Against the London the dark bishop comes out before the queen's knight: it stands opposite the London bishop, and if White takes, the London player's favourite piece is gone.

quiz.label: C-pawn first
quiz.note: When White's queen takes back, the c-pawn goes before the e-pawn. It shuts out the queen check that would win your b-pawn, and it starts the same triangle as in the Slav.

units.title: The Caro-Kann
units.kicker: Black · a second answer to the e-pawn
units.why: Two pawn moves start every game: c-pawn one square, d-pawn two. Then the light bishop comes out before the e-pawn moves, the same idea as the Slav setup against the d-pawn.

idea.t: The c-pawn backs up the d-pawn, and the road for your light bishop stays open. Now White has to decide about the e-pawn: push it past, trade it, or guard it.

idea.h: Pushed past: bishop out, then hit the chain
idea.t: The bishop leaves before your e-pawn closes the door. Then the e-pawn one square, and the c-pawn two squares at the pawn that holds White's chain together.

idea.h: Traded: both knights before the bishop
idea.t: Take back with the c-pawn. With the c-pawns gone, White's queen can come out at your b-pawn the moment the bishop leaves, so the knights come first. The same rule as the Slav pawn trade.

idea.h: Guarded: take, then the bishop with a hit
idea.t: Take the e-pawn and bring the bishop out at the knight. When the knight steps aside and hits the bishop, step back one square and keep the diagonal.
Queen's knight, e-pawn, king's knight, dark bishop, castle. The queen's knight goes first because it covers the middle square White's knight wants.

idea.h: A free pawn, one game in three
idea.t: A third of club players guard the knight with the bishop. That bishop now stands between White's queen and the d-pawn, so your queen takes it.

quiz.label: Bishop out first
quiz.note: The whole point of the opening: the bishop leaves before the e-pawn shuts the door. Then e-pawn, then the c-pawn two squares.

quiz.label: C-pawn two squares
quiz.note: It hits the pawn that holds White's chain together. Queen's knight behind it next.

quiz.label: King's knight
quiz.note: Both knights are out. Now the bishop can go.

quiz.label: Step back
quiz.rule: Step back, then the queen's knight
quiz.note: The bishop stays on its diagonal. From here the order is: queen's knight, e-pawn, king's knight.

quiz.label: Take the d-pawn
quiz.rule: Bishop guards the knight: take the d-pawn
quiz.note: The bishop stepped in front of the queen, so nothing guards it. A clean pawn.

quiz.label: Make room
quiz.rule: H-pawn comes: make room for the bishop
quiz.note: One square for the edge pawn gives the bishop a way back.

units.title: Spot the threat
units.why: In 23 of your last 28 losses there was at least one moment like this: a piece left hanging, or a threat you didn't look for. Every position here is from your own games, at the moment it went wrong.

idea.h: What did their last move attack?
idea.t: Before you touch a piece, look at the move your opponent just made and everything it now hits. Here the knight attacked your queen.

idea.h: Can my piece be taken where it lands?
idea.t: Then check your own move. Here the queen had to move, and it went to a square a knight covered (blue: your move, red: the reply).
Last, look at every check your opponent has. Here the new queen didn't matter: the checks came first, and they ended the game.

units.title: Against the Italian
units.why: Your best e-pawn opening as Black: ten wins in fifteen games. It is also the home of the setup you will use everywhere: knight out, bishop to its diagonal, castle.

idea.t: Your bishop goes to the same kind of diagonal as White's and aims at f2, the pawn beside White's king.
When White pushes the d-pawn, take it, then check with the bishop. Stepping back would give the pawns time to roll.
After the bishops come off, your d-pawn hits the center before White's pawns can advance.
Your rook now guards f7 and your king has stepped away. Next the h-pawn kicks the knight back home.

quiz.label: Mirror the bishop
quiz.note: Your bishop goes to the same diagonal and aims at f2.

quiz.label: Bishop check
quiz.note: Check first, then trade bishops. Retreating gives the center time to roll.

quiz.label: The d-pawn strikes
quiz.note: The point of the whole line: hit the center before White's pawns can roll. It hits the bishop too.

quiz.label: Knight grabs the e-pawn
quiz.note: Take it. Your knight also hits the knight that blocks the check.

quiz.label: Small d-pawn move
quiz.note: Your e-pawn is guarded for good. Same setup every time.

quiz.label: Castle
quiz.note: Your rook now guards f7 and your king is out of the line of fire.

units.title: The Sicilian
units.kicker: White · same plan as your Italian
units.why: About one White game in seven, and you have lost more of them than you have won. The plan is your Italian plan: the small c-pawn move, then the big center.

idea.t: As in your Italian, the c-pawn gets ready for the d-pawn push. Two pawns in the middle are coming.

idea.h: A knight in front of your pawn? Push it
idea.t: Black's knight stands where your d-pawn can hit it. Push, then push again with the f-pawn and the e-pawn.

idea.h: Push the knights off the board
idea.t: Every pawn push kicks a knight. Black's pieces run out of squares.
If the queen grabs your d-pawn, take the knight with check first. When the pawn takes back, your queen takes Black's.

quiz.label: Small pawn move
quiz.rule: Small pawn move, like the Italian
quiz.note: The same idea as your Italian: get ready to push the d-pawn and stand two pawns in the center.

quiz.label: Push past the knight
quiz.rule: Knight in front of your pawn? Push it
quiz.note: Kick the knight out of the center. You skipped this against three opponents.

quiz.label: Kick it again
quiz.note: Your f-pawn chases the knight. It is running out of squares.

quiz.label: Now the other knight
quiz.note: Push again and hit Black's other knight. Black's pieces are being pushed off the board.

quiz.label: Take the knight with check
quiz.note: Check first. When the pawn takes back, Black's queen has no defender.

units.title: Scotch & center gambits
units.why: Thirteen games and only four wins: your weakest Black opening. Now it is your Italian setup: the bishop goes straight to its diagonal, the queen joins it against f2, and against the gambits you develop instead of grabbing a second pawn.

idea.t: When White takes back with the knight, your bishop goes straight to its Italian diagonal. It hits the knight in the middle and aims at f2. A check first only costs a move.

idea.h: Knight trade? The queen joins in
idea.t: Queen and bishop both hit f2 and mate is threatened. White has to spend a move on it; then your d-pawn takes back toward the middle and you castle long.
Taking the second pawn lets White's bishop take on f7 and the queen win your bishop back with check. It happened twice. Bring the knight out and you are in your Italian.
Don't take the second pawn here either. The d-pawn strike opens the center for your pieces and leaves White with a lone pawn in the middle.

quiz.label: Bishop to its diagonal
quiz.note: The same square as in your Italian. It hits the knight in the middle and aims at f2. Don't check first: the bishop ends up here anyway, a move later.

quiz.label: Queen hits f2
quiz.note: Queen and bishop both aim at f2: mate is threatened. White has to deal with it before anything else.

quiz.label: D-pawn takes back
quiz.note: Toward the middle: your other bishop gets its road and the d-file opens for your rook.

quiz.label: Queen joins in
quiz.note: Now the knight in the middle is hit three times.

quiz.label: Knight out, not the second pawn
quiz.rule: Develop, don't take a second pawn
quiz.note: Develop. Taking the c-pawn walks into the bishop sacrifice on f7, as against themobun.

quiz.label: The d-pawn strikes
quiz.rule: Danish: hit back with the d-pawn
quiz.note: Don't take the second pawn. Hit back in the center. Against yonatha32 you took it and White's pieces came out with tempo.

units.title: The Caro-Kann
units.kicker: White · two lines cover most games
units.why: About one White game in seven, and you win two in three. Two lines cover most of them: the h-pawn march and the knight trade.

idea.t: Black's bishop comes out early. Your knight steps back and attacks it.
The pawn threatens to trap the bishop. Later it cramps Black's whole kingside.
Swap off Black's best piece, put your king on the other side, and attack where your h-pawn already stands.
Taking with check spoils Black's pawns. Stepping back, as you did in your games, gave Black an easy game.

quiz.label: Knight guards the pawn
quiz.note: Defend with a piece. You played this in all 13 games; keep doing it.

quiz.label: Knight hits the bishop
quiz.note: Step back with tempo. The bishop must move again.

quiz.label: Push the h-pawn at the bishop
quiz.rule: Push the h-pawn at the bishop
quiz.note: The pawn threatens to keep going and trap the bishop. Black has to answer it.

quiz.label: Pawn forward again
quiz.note: Kick the bishop to the edge. Your pawn now cramps Black's whole kingside.

quiz.label: Offer the bishop trade
quiz.note: Your bishop meets Black's best piece. Trading it leaves Black passive.

quiz.label: Take the knight
quiz.note: Trade with check. Black has to take back with a pawn and spoil the pawn structure. Your old move, stepping back, gave Black an easy game.

units.title: Against the Ruy Lopez
units.why: The same setup as your Italian: hit the e-pawn with the knight, bishop to its diagonal, castle. You have won seven of ten here.

idea.t: Your knight attacks White's center pawn at once.

idea.h: Bishop out, as in the Italian
idea.t: Same diagonal, aimed at f2. Castle next.
After the bishop takes your knight, take back with the d-pawn. If the knight grabs your pawn, your queen hits the knight and the e-pawn at once.

quiz.label: Knight hits the e-pawn
quiz.note: The Berlin. Go after White's e-pawn at once.

quiz.label: Bishop out, as in the Italian
quiz.rule: White castled: bishop out, as in the Italian
quiz.note: Same diagonal as in your Italian, aimed at f2. Castle next.

quiz.label: Bishop steps back
quiz.note: It keeps its diagonal toward White's king. About equal: White has more center, you have easy development.

quiz.label: Bishop to the Italian diagonal
quiz.note: Same square as in your Italian, aimed at f2. You won both games where you played it.

quiz.label: Take toward the center
quiz.note: Your queen and bishop open up at once. Against vasylsaienko the b-pawn took and your bishop was lost four moves later.

quiz.label: Queen fork
quiz.note: Your queen hits the knight and the e-pawn.

units.title: Finish the job
units.why: 21 of your 91 losses came after you had been winning by a lot. Every position here is one of those games, at the move where it slipped. Find the move that keeps the win.

idea.t: You were winning, and the queen had mate in one (green). In the game a pawn move came instead (blue). When you are ahead, look at every check you have before anything else.
The queen grabbed a pawn (blue) and Black developed with a hit on it. The last piece out (green) was stronger: it also stops Black from castling.

idea.h: What does their next move pin?
idea.t: The bishop stepped back (blue) and Black's bishop pinned your queen to your king (red). Trading that bishop, or stepping the king into the corner first, kept the win.

units.title: Two Knights & the third-move tricks
units.why: You have won eight of nine when Black brings the second knight out. Keep it that way, and know the two traps Black sets on move three.

idea.t: Your knight and bishop both hit f7, and only the king defends it.
If Black takes back with the knight, sacrifice on f7. The fork forces the king to take, and then it is out in the open.
Black leaves the center pawn hanging on purpose. Trade knights; never grab the pawn.

quiz.label: Knight jumps at f7
quiz.note: Your knight and bishop both hit f7, and only the king defends it.

quiz.label: Knight takes f7
quiz.note: The Fried Liver sacrifice. Your knight forks the queen and rook, so the king has to take.

quiz.label: Queen check
quiz.note: Check, and your queen piles on the pinned knight.

quiz.label: Bishop check
quiz.rule: Knight to the rim: bishop check
quiz.note: Keep the bishop alive with check.

quiz.label: Take with the bishop
quiz.note: Safe and simple: Black's king loses castling rights and you are a pawn up.

quiz.label: Trade knights
quiz.rule: Knight jumps in: trade, never grab
quiz.note: Simple and good. Don't take the center pawn.

units.title: Vienna & early attacks
units.kicker: Black · knights first, then the bishop
units.why: Nineteen games between them and only seven wins. Against the early bishop and the f-pawn gambits it is your setup again: knight out first, then the bishop to its diagonal. Against the early queen the bishop goes next to your king.

idea.t: Against the early bishop your knight comes out before your bishop. It covers the square White's queen wants, so the raid on your g-pawn never comes.
Now the bishop goes to its usual diagonal and aims at f2. It is your Italian setup with the knights already out.
Against the f-pawn gambits your bishop takes the diagonal White's king needs. White can't castle short, and grabbing your e-pawn opens the king up.
If the f-pawn grabs your e-pawn, the queen checks, then takes the e-pawn with check and hits the rook in the corner.

idea.h: Early queen? Bishop by the king
idea.t: Against the early queen, block f7 with the pawn and the knight. Then the bishop goes behind the pawn, where it guards your knight for good.

quiz.label: Knight out first
quiz.note: The knight covers the square White's queen wants. Against irekmary the bishop came out first and White's queen hit your g-pawn.

quiz.label: Now the bishop
quiz.rule: Then the bishop to its diagonal
quiz.note: Your usual diagonal, aimed at f2. The knight already covers the square the queen wanted.

quiz.label: Bishop out, don't take
quiz.note: Your usual diagonal. White's king can't castle short now, and grabbing your e-pawn opens lines toward it.

quiz.label: Bishop out, don't take
quiz.note: Your usual diagonal. White's king can't castle short while the bishop eyes its path, and the e-pawn is poisoned.

quiz.label: Queen check
quiz.rule: Pawn grabbed: queen check wins a rook
quiz.note: With the f-pawn gone, White's king has no cover.

quiz.label: Bishop next to your king
quiz.rule: Bishop by the king: it guards the knight
quiz.note: From here it guards your knight. In both October losses the bishop went to the Italian diagonal, and White's queen and bishop won the knight.

units.title: Philidor & Petrov
units.kicker: White · hit the center at once
units.why: About one White game in seven. Hit the center at once, and know the two shots: the bishop on f7 and the queen on the open file.

idea.t: Against the small d-pawn defence, push your d-pawn two squares. Black has to give up the center or stay cramped.
When Black wastes a move, the bishop takes f7, and after the king takes, your knight grabs the center pawn with check.
If Black copies you, your queen hits the knight, and any knight move lets your own knight move with discovered check.

quiz.label: Hit the center at once
quiz.note: Push the d-pawn two. Black's center pawn is attacked again and your bishop's diagonal opens.

quiz.label: Knight takes back
quiz.note: Your knight lands in the center. You already have more space.

quiz.label: Bishop at f7
quiz.rule: Bishop at f7; watch for the sacrifice
quiz.note: Of course. The bishop aims at f7, and you can take the center pawn whenever you like.

quiz.label: Bishop takes f7!
quiz.note: The sacrifice. If the king takes, your knight takes the e-pawn with check. You had this shot against Nona_Zulfa on Oct 14 and played a quiet bishop move instead.

quiz.label: Take the pawn
quiz.note: Take first. Black can win your pawn back, but only with the right move.

quiz.label: Queen to the e-file
quiz.rule: Queen to the e-file: the copycat trap
quiz.note: Your queen hits Black's knight. And if that knight ever steps away, your knight moves with discovered check.

units.title: The d-pawn: White's other tries
units.kicker: Black · same setup, a few tricks
units.why: The rest of the d-pawn openings you meet. The setup does not change, and in two of these lessons White's most natural move hands you material.

idea.t: When White's bishop comes out at your knight, jump to the middle. After the natural e-pawn move, the queen checks and takes the bishop.

idea.h: Take the c-pawn and hold it
idea.t: With both White knights out, take the pawn and guard it with the b-pawn.
When the bishop takes your knight, the e-pawn takes back. Your king stays safe and the dark bishop gets a clear road.

quiz.label: Knight jumps to the middle
quiz.rule: Bishop comes at your knight: jump to the middle
quiz.note: It steps away from the bishop and attacks White's knight.

quiz.label: Queen check wins the bishop
quiz.note: Check, and the queen attacks the bishop at the same time. White can block the check but not save both.

quiz.label: Take the c-pawn
quiz.rule: Both knights out: take the c-pawn
quiz.note: If White wins it back slowly, your bishop comes out. If White pushes the e-pawn, your b-pawn holds the extra pawn.

quiz.label: Guard it from the edge
quiz.rule: Knight jumps at your c-pawn: guard it from the edge
quiz.note: The only good move: the knight guards the c-pawn's square. Everything else loses material.

quiz.label: Take back with the e-pawn
quiz.note: Your king stays safe and the dark bishop gets a clear road.

units.title: Scandinavian, Pirc & French
units.why: Three defences that make up nearly a third of your White games. You win two in three of them; one plan for each keeps it that way.

idea.t: Develop with a threat. Every queen move is a move Black isn't developing.
Never with the queen: the queens come off and your lead in development is gone.
Against the fianchetto, trade off Black's bishop and push the h-pawn at the king.

idea.h: Push past and lock the center
idea.t: Your pawn cramps Black's kingside. Support the chain from behind with the c-pawn, as in your Italian.

quiz.label: Hit the queen
quiz.note: Develop with tempo. Every queen move is a move Black isn't developing.

quiz.label: Block with the bishop
quiz.rule: Block the check with the bishop, never the queen
quiz.note: Not with the queen. Against FernandoUK you blocked with the queen, the queens came off, and you lost a long ending. The bishop keeps your lead in development.

quiz.label: Big center
quiz.rule: Big center; skip the pawn gambit
quiz.note: This is the move. Your pawn gambit here is in its own lesson, with the reason to drop it.

quiz.label: Bishop to the attack
quiz.note: Your bishop and queen are about to line up against Black's king.

quiz.label: Push past
quiz.rule: Push past and lock the center
quiz.note: Lock the center. Your pawn cramps Black's kingside, and Black's light bishop is stuck behind its pawns.

quiz.label: Support from behind
quiz.note: The same small pawn move as in your Italian and Sicilian.

units.title: Endings
units.why: 83 of your games reached an ending with you level or better, and 28 of those were lost. These are the moves that decided them: back ranks, pawn endings and active rooks.

idea.t: Rooks on the board and no square for your king. Before any rook move, check their checks on your back rank: here one rook move (blue) let the other rook in with mate (red).
In a pawn ending one trade decides it. Taking (blue) gave Black a passed pawn far from your king; pushing past (green) kept the draw.
Your rook could cut White's king off (green), or your king could walk up to help the passed pawn. The rook went back to defend (blue), and White's pawns got going.

units.title: Other first moves
units.why: The c-pawn, the knight first, a fianchetto. Take the center and the setup you know follows.

idea.t: Take the center, just like against the e-pawn. Knights out, bishop out at the knight, castle.
The d-pawn goes to the middle and the same setup follows: c-pawn, bishop out, then the e-pawn.

quiz.label: E-pawn two squares
quiz.note: Take the center, just like against the e-pawn.

quiz.label: Bishop hits the knight
quiz.note: Next it can take it and leave White with doubled pawns.

quiz.label: E-pawn kicks the knight
quiz.note: Equal, and you have space.

quiz.label: D-pawn to the middle
quiz.note: The same start as against the d-pawn. Your Slav setup follows.

quiz.label: C-pawn one square
quiz.note: Blunts the long-diagonal bishop.

units.title: Rare first moves
units.why: Rare, but one of them cost you a game in six moves. Guard the e-pawn first, then play normal chess.

idea.t: Black's bishop aims at your e-pawn from far away. Defend it with your bishop before anything else.
The knight-first move usually turns into positions you already know.

quiz.label: Bishop guards the e-pawn
quiz.rule: Guard your e-pawn with the bishop
quiz.note: Defend it with a bishop first. Against Gilmarmv the pawn fell when your bishop went elsewhere, and the game lasted six moves.

quiz.label: Queen guards
quiz.note: Now the e-pawn is safe for good. Castle next.

quiz.note: This is your Italian.
